bach_leipzig_late_quill.name: bach_leipzig_late_quill
bach_leipzig_late_quill.description: J.S. Bach's dense, energetic late Leipzig cantata hand: broad goose quill, dramatic thick-thin contrast, steep rightward slant, hooked C-rests, and dark iron-gall sepia.
bach_leipzig_late_quill.paleography_notes: Models J.S. Bach's late Leipzig composing scores (1723-1750, weekly cantatas and St. Matthew Passion revisions): sharply cut broad goose quill (43 deg, 0.14 min-ratio) producing extreme hairline-to-downstroke contrast and rich iron-gall pooling, steep 15.5 deg forward impetus, compact wedge/teardrop noteheads, dominant Baroque hooked C-quarter rests, economical dense contrapuntal spacing with end-of-bar cramming, and oxidized dark sepia iron-gall ink with moderate bleed-through on Leipzig rag paper.

handel_london_opera_rush.name: handel_london_opera_rush
handel_london_opera_rush.description: G.F. Handel's fast London opera composing drafts: bold wide strokes, generous barline overshoots, open sweeping noteheads, and rapid end-of-bar cramming.
handel_london_opera_rush.paleography_notes: Models G.F. Handel's rapid London Royal Academy and Covent Garden opera autographs (e.g., Giulio Cesare, Orlando, Messiah working drafts): broad muscular quill cut yielding thick bold strokes and heavy ink pooling, large open sweeping oval noteheads with frequent unclosed hollow heads, sweeping barline overshoots across staves, vigorous horizontal momentum with rapid end-of-bar cramming, and frequent marginal character/tempo cues on oblong Dutch-laid English rag paper.

vivaldi_venetian_furia.name: vivaldi_venetian_furia
vivaldi_venetian_furia.description: Antonio Vivaldi's famously rapid Venetian shorthand: slashing diagonal noteheads, steep wild beams, dry-brush iron-gall skips, and crowded measures.
vivaldi_venetian_furia.paleography_notes: Models Antonio Vivaldi's rapid Venetian working scores in the Turin Foa and Giordano collections (Ospedale della Pieta concertos): fine flexible quill driven at high speed causing dry-brush iron-gall skips and wide ink variation, steep 17.5 deg forward slant, slashing diagonal noteheads (-42 deg), spiky minimal Italian shorthand rests, generous barline overshoots, crowded variable measures with severe end-of-bar cramming, and wavy sloped rastrum staves on warm Venetian rag paper.

telemann_hamburg_fair_copy.name: telemann_hamburg_fair_copy
telemann_hamburg_fair_copy.description: G.P. Telemann's clean, balanced engraver-ready fair copies: neat oval noteheads, gentle nib contrast, and airy consistent spacing.
telemann_hamburg_fair_copy.paleography_notes: Models Georg Philipp Telemann's famously legible Hamburg fair copies and self-engraved Tafelmusik / Der getreue Musik-Meister exemplars: evenly cut medium quill with gentle nib contrast (0.34 min-ratio) and steady ink flow, neat poised oval noteheads, graceful Baroque C-hook and calligraphic S-curl rests, refined ornate clefs, restrained barlines, and airy, engraver-ready horizontal spacing on clean cream Hamburg laid paper.

haydn_esterhazy_copyist.name: haydn_esterhazy_copyist
haydn_esterhazy_copyist.description: 18th-century Austrian Esterhazy court copyist: crisp dark brown ink on cream rag paper, formal ornate clefs, and slightly sloped hand-ruled rastrum staves.
haydn_esterhazy_copyist.paleography_notes: Models professional Esterhazy court Kopisten (e.g., Joseph Elssler Sr., Johann Radnitzky) preparing archival parts and scores for Joseph Haydn at Eisenstadt and Eszterhaza: crisp dark walnut-brown iron-gall ink on warm Austrian cream rag paper, sharp broad-edge quill discipline, formal ornate Viennese G/C/F clefs, transitional 18th-century mix of backward-7 and Baroque C-hook quarter rests, tidy measured bar spacing, and characteristic slightly sloped 5-nib hand-ruled rastrum staves.

mozart_vienna_autograph_ink.name: mozart_vienna_autograph_ink
mozart_vienna_autograph_ink.description: W.A. Mozart's late Vienna ink-pen fluency: nimble fine-medium nib, graceful forward slant, distinctive backward-7 quarter rests, and airy balanced bars.
mozart_vienna_autograph_ink.paleography_notes: Models W.A. Mozart's late Viennese autographs (1784-1791: Le nozze di Figaro, Don Giovanni, late piano concertos, Jupiter Symphony): nimble fine-medium quill nib with fluid chestnut-sepia iron-gall ink, graceful 14.5 deg forward cursive slant, compact poised teardrop noteheads, signature Viennese backward-7 quarter rests (dominant weight 0.58), elegant calligraphic clefs, and airy, remarkably balanced measure planning across 12-stave Viennese oblong rag paper.
